clue.text: Heart of whodunit with blurb about assault

indicators.note: the heart of anything is its centre, so only the central letters of the word are kept
to turn about is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the fourth and fifth letters of this eight-letter word sit at its centre
a puff is a piece of promotional praise, like the blurb on a book jacket

explanation.surface: A crime novel whose central plot involves an assault, plus some publicity copy on the cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of whodunit' sounds like the crux of a mystery plot, but it just takes the two central letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Duff up is British slang for beating someone, a physical attack, which is what an assault is.

clue.text: Understand, after 12th month, Apple product no longer on insurance, essentially

indicators.note: something no longer on has been taken off, so two letters are removed from the word
the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: December is the twelfth month, abbreviated DEC
the iPhone is made by Apple; taking out ON leaves these four letters
the fifth of nine letters is the middle one

explanation.surface: Someone works out that their Apple phone is no longer covered by insurance after December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer on' reads as a lapsed policy, but it tells you to remove the letters O and N from the phone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To decipher a code or scrawl is to make sense of it, which is a common synonym of understanding.

clue.text: In Florida, a solicitor’s using every effort

blocks.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Florida
taken as written
a tout solicits custom, pestering people to buy

explanation.surface: A hard-working lawyer in Florida is giving a case everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it is simply someone who solicits business, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: Going flat out means working at maximum speed or exertion, an idiom for trying as hard as possible.

clue.text: Adolescent a little tempted to get into speed after university — the latest of many

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small piece of it, here its opening letter
getting into something means going inside it, so one set of letters sits within another
coming after something means following it, so the earlier-clued piece is placed second

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
miles per hour, a unit of speed
a teen is a teenager
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A teenager, slightly tempted, speeds off after university, the latest in a long line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' is not a verb here but a unit abbreviation, which opens up to hold the young person and the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteenth describes the most recent in a very large, uncounted series of occurrences.

clue.text: A way into reconditioned aircraft business

indicators.note: a reconditioned engine has been taken apart and rebuilt, so these letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written
via means by way of, and a via is a road in Latin
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A route into the business of refurbishing old aeroplanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a connecting word but is the fodder; 'reconditioned aircraft' reads as one phrase, yet the adjective belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviation is the industry and activity of designing, building and flying planes.

clue.text: Terminal velocity at the start — speed of sound during echo — it’s often observed on railway platform

definitions.text: it’s often observed on railway platform

blocks.note: V is the symbol for velocity in physics
a terminal point is an ending
Mach numbers measure speed against the speed of sound
in the course of, as in 'in the night'
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Physics jargon about terminal velocity and sound echoing along a railway platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal velocity' is a physics term, but it splits: terminal is its own chunk with the V at its start. 'During echo' is not a container but two plain chunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Snack and drink dispensers are a familiar fixture on station platforms, so this is a descriptive definition by example.

clue.text: Dismay of apprentice meeting Alan half-cut

indicators.note: cutting something in half removes half of it, so only the first two of four letters remain

blocks.note: the first three letters, used as a short form of the word
the first half of the name

explanation.surface: A trainee is dismayed to find his colleague Alan rather drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-cut is British slang for tipsy, which the surface uses; in the wordplay it literally halves the name.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to shock and horrify them, a synonym of the verb to dismay.

clue.text: Gather detailed quantity of paper before end of day for hearing

indicators.note: de-tailed means with its tail removed, so the final letter is dropped
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to gather in a harvest is to bring it in
a quire is 24 or 25 sheets of paper; its final E goes
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone collects a detailed stack of paperwork before the day ends, ready for a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as thorough, but means cut off at the tail. A quire is a traditional measure of paper sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A public inquiry is an official investigation where evidence is heard, so it is a kind of formal hearing.

clue.text: Require limousine on vacation to see obelisk

indicators.note: a vacated building is emptied, so the word loses all its inside letters and keeps its ends

blocks.note: to require is to need
just the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tourist on holiday wants a limo to go and see a famous monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' pretends to be a holiday; it empties the word. Cleopatra's Needle is a famous obelisk on the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall tapering stone pillars are often called needles, as with Cleopatra's Needle in London and New York.

clue.text: Spitting Image showing trick photography

blocks.note: someone's spitting image is their double, an exact lookalike
a showing or display of something is an exposure

explanation.surface: The satirical puppet show Spitting Image uses camera trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV show of grotesque puppets of public figures; the capital letters disguise the ordinary phrase meaning a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing the same frame twice superimposes two images, a classic camera effect for ghosts and twins.

clue.text: Vice squad ultimately have restraint

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: a vice is a workshop clamp
the final letter
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: The vice squad in the end show restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice squad' is a police unit, but vice here is the workbench tool that grips things.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a firm official curb on some activity, so it is a form of restriction or control.

clue.text: Expressed the most annoyance

indicators.note: to express something is to put it into words out loud, so we go by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: the peak is the highest point, the most there is

explanation.surface: Someone voiced the greatest irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expressed the most annoyance' reads as a complaint, but splits into a sound indicator, a phrase meaning maximum, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of irritation or resentment, typically from wounded pride.

clue.text: Saw hype about book

blocks.note: PR, public relations, is the business of hype
a quarrel over money is one about money
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed the promotional fuss surrounding a new book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; it is the noun for an old saying. 'About' is a letter chunk, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old-fashioned word for a traditional saying or maxim, which is what a proverb is.

clue.text: Opposition and I pass on taking 50-50

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it, so one set of letters goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, twice
to will property is to pass it on to heirs

explanation.surface: Faced with resistance, someone declines an even-chance bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' suggests declining, but here it means bequeath; I and WILL hold the two fifties between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility or animosity towards someone, so it matches opposition in the sense of antagonism.

clue.text: Oddly missing penalties — initially Neymar scoffed

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters gone, only the even-positioned letters are left
initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Neymar, the Brazilian footballer, strangely misses penalties and is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' in the surface means jeered at, but the definition is the British sense of gobbled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff is British slang for eating greedily, so scoffed food has been consumed.

clue.text: English agree to swap sides, yet mostly will display great acuity

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, so one letter standing for one side is exchanged for the other
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
R for right becomes L for left
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: The English agree to change allegiance, but will mostly show great sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swap sides' sounds like defection; in the wordplay R (right) turns into L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle eye is exceptionally keen vision or watchfulness, like that of the bird of prey.

clue.text: Doctor tries net to describe current inflammation

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order
to describe a circle is to draw round it, so these letters go around another

blocks.note: eight letters to be rearranged
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A physician attempts to use a net to describe a current case of inflammation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describe' means draw round, a geometry sense, so the rearranged letters wrap round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis is inflammation of the intestine, so the answer is a specific kind of inflammation.

clue.text: Extremely hot suit

blocks.note: something hot is fashionable, or in
spades is one of the four card suits

explanation.surface: A suit that is very hot to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely hot' reads as one phrase, but the first word is the definition and the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something in spades is an idiom for having it in great abundance or to a very high degree.

clue.text: Stoppage of vital functions — heard about cure in the East?

indicators.note: what is heard is taken by its sound, not its spelling
about means around, so one set of letters encircles another

blocks.note: to fix a problem is to cure it; this spelling sounds identical
the East is Asia, the place something is in

explanation.surface: Someone hears about an Eastern remedy for a medical emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound-alike chunk takes an unusual spelling so the answer can be written correctly; the continent wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphyxia is suffocation from lack of oxygen, which halts breathing and other life processes.

clue.text: Pen point in command — producing drawing together

blocks.note: a pen for pigs is a sty
PT is the abbreviation for point
IC stands for in charge, that is in command

explanation.surface: A nib, under instruction, produces a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen point' and 'drawing' paint a picture of sketching; pen is an animal enclosure and drawing means contracting.
explanation.definitionFit: A styptic substance contracts tissue and blood vessels to stop bleeding, an astringent that pulls things tight.

clue.text: Any of these five school staff coach set sequence

blocks.note: to school someone is to teach or drill them
a retinue of attendants following a dignitary
to coach an athlete is to prepare them
a set of connected wheels or gears in a mechanism
a series of connected events or thoughts

explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists five separate meanings of one word; 'school staff coach' tempts you to read it as a school bus.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean teaching, a retinue, a railway carriage chain, a gear set, and a connected series of things.

clue.text: For example, the nickel citrate sample is used up

indicators.note: a sample is a small portion taken from something larger, so the letters come from within the words
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of one word and most of the next

explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is itself an example of the answer in grammar, the definite one.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, 'the' is the definite article, so it is an instance of this part of speech.

clue.text: Move to avoid start of tennis match, drinking whiskey

indicators.note: someone drinking takes something in, so one letter goes inside the others

blocks.note: every point in tennis begins with a serve
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of tennis' tempts you to take the letter T; the whole phrase is SERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to change direction suddenly to get out of the way of something.

clue.text: Respect African country — as Trump might say, it’s ‘great’

blocks.note: in every respect means in every way

explanation.surface: Donald Trump praising an African nation as great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As Trump might say' flags an Americanism: the phrase is US congratulation.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English this exclamation means well done, an expression of approval for an achievement.

clue.text: Smell‘s old and unfriendly

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A smell that is stale and unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' is simply the join between the two chunks.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent, especially a noticeable or unpleasant one, which is what a smell is.

clue.text: Sort of car‘s difficult as far as parking

blocks.note: hard means difficult
as in 'up to the gate', as far as the gate

explanation.walkthrough: 'As far as' is a single chunk meaning TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid metal roof, as opposed to a soft-top convertible.

clue.text: Old-fashioned cabaret routine’s attributes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-fashioned' could describe the cabaret, but it is the definition, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a style that deliberately imitates the fashions of the recent past.

clue.text: Overlooked German and put warning inside

indicators.note: to put one thing somewhere is to place it, here within the others as the next word says

explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked has gone unseen or been missed, which is exactly what unnoticed means.

clue.text: Took out key dictionary to grasp right tense

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold in the hand, so one pair of letters is gripped inside another word

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.walkthrough: 'Took out' looks like removing, but means took someone on a date; OED holds R and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone out, as on a date, is to escort them, accompanying them somewhere socially.

clue.text: Estate Tax not quite covering debt at the end

indicators.note: not quite all of something is a little short, so the final letter is dropped
the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: to assess is to levy a tax; one letter is removed
the final letter of the word
